questions.qtext: Find the number of quadrilaterals in the given figure.
questions.solution:
2-digit quadrilateral = (4, 5) ⇒ 1
3-digit quadrilateral = (4, 5, 6), (4, 5, 8), (3, 4, 5), (1, 4, 5) ⇒ 4
4-digit quadrilateral = (1, 2, 3, 4), (5, 6, 7, 8), (3, 4, 5, 6), (1, 4, 5, 8), (1, 4, 5, 6), (3, 4, 5, 8) ⇒ 6
Hence, total quadrilateral in the figure = 1 + 4 + 6 = 11

questions.qtext:
A team of four students has to be made for inter-school carrom competition from three boys:
Akash, Bharat, Chandra and three Girls: Deepa, Eva, Farah; such that Akash and Eva should never be together. If and only if Farah is selected then Chandra is selected. In how many ways can the team be selected such that exactly 2 boys are selected?
questions.solution:
If Akash is selected then Eva cannot be selected. If Farah is there, then Chandra, must be in the team.
Let Akash, Bharat, Chandra, Deepa, Eva and Farah be denoted by A, B, C, D, E and F respectively.
Then possible ways can be
B C D F
B C E F
A C D F only

questions.qtext: Select the most suitable sentence with respect to grammar and usage:

options.text: A team of graduate students are going to Agra to see the Taj Mahal.
A team of graduate student are going to Agra to see the Taj Mahal.
A team of graduate students were going to Agra to see the Taj Mahal.
A team of graduate students is going to Agra to see the Taj Mahal.

questions.solution:
Option (a) is wrong because the verb should be singular.
'A team of graduate student' is a wrong phrase so option (b) is wrong.
Option (c) is wrong because it also has verb error.
Thus option (d) is the best option choice.
